doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Phineas Newborn's neglect and Mabern's personal philosophy
summary: He calls Phineas Newborn the most underrated musician and says he ignores critics because he is pure of heart.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: two right hands.” Tommy Flanagan loved him. Ahmad Jamal loved him. But they really dogged him, just to tell you the truth, that you know, and hopefully one day, I don’t know how, something can be done. Because he should be alive and well but he was heartbroken you see. So if you’re not tough-skinned out there, between the system and some of the critics and some of the musicians, and you can listen to what they said and believe it, hey may you’ll go under. But I refuse to let them to that to me. I say, “Well thank you very much, you’re entitled to your opinion.” Because I’m not saying anybody’s got to be a Harold Mabern fan, you know, so I just do what I do and if I’m honest, and if I’m okay with it most of the time, and if I’m not okay with you then it’s your problem, you know. I’m not perfect but I’m pure of heart. And that’s the philosophy that I live by. You know what I’m saying.
